title: Invertibility of the principal reduction comparison on flat models
statement: In the exact-sections principal-quotient setup of [lem-pod-derived-reduction-sheaf-resolution-independence], assume R is a domain and t≠0. For every K-flat sheaf complex P with flat terms, the canonical comparison alpha_P from derived quotient of sections to sections of derived quotient is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; principal quotient specialization of the original item proof

proof.text: Tensor the coefficient short exact sequence with each flat sheaf term. Apply exact sections. The first map remains injective, so multiplication by t is injective on each section module.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; principal quotient specialization of the original item proof

proof.text: Choose a flat-term ordinary K-flat resolution of the section complex. Its terms are torsion-free over the domain, so t is injective on them. Principal quotient preserves its augmentation quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; principal quotient specialization of the original item proof

proof.text: The mixed-tensor counit is invertible on this ordinary K-flat model. Its naturality and the invertible quotient augmentation imply invertibility on the section complex. The other factors of alpha are the quotient-section isomorphism and the K-flat sheaf counit.
